statement: Intravenous thrombolysis (alteplase) given within ~3 hours of ischemic stroke onset improves 3-month functional outcomes; the window extends to 4.5 hours and, in imaging-selected patients, out to 24 hours.
effect_size: NINDS: absolute increase in favorable outcome; HOPE 2025 extended benefit to selected 4.5-24h patients
population: Acute ischemic stroke adults (NINDS 1995; ECASS-3; HOPE 2025)

provenance.primary: NINDS rt-PA Stroke Study Group - 'Tissue plasminogen activator for acute ischemic stroke', NEJM 1995
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (HOPE: Zhou 2025 10.1001/jama.2025.12063)

confidence_notes: Time-dependent and modeled '~1.9M neurons/min' framing is mechanistic. Benefit is real but window- and access-limited; intracerebral hemorrhage must be excluded by CT first (thrombolysis is harmful in hemorrhagic stroke).

statement: Endovascular thrombectomy for large-vessel-occlusion ischemic stroke roughly doubles the odds of functional independence, with a number-needed-to-treat of about 2.6 - one of the best NNTs in medicine.
effect_size: Pooled cOR 2.49 for reduced disability; NNT ~2.6 for one less disabled patient (HERMES)
population: 1287 patients, 5 RCTs, large-vessel occlusion (HERMES individual-patient-data meta-analysis)

provenance.primary: Goyal M, et al. - 'Endovascular thrombectomy after large-vessel ischaemic stroke: a meta-analysis of individual patient data from five randomised trials', Lancet 2016
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Window later extended to 24h in imaging-selected patients (DAWN, DEFUSE-3). Main real-world limit is access to comprehensive stroke centers.

statement: Most strokes are preventable upstream: blood-pressure control is the single largest modifiable risk factor, and anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation cuts AF-related stroke by roughly 60-70%.
effect_size: Anticoagulation: ~64% relative risk reduction in AF stroke (warfarin meta-analyses); BP lowering largest population-attributable lever
population: Adults with hypertension / atrial fibrillation

provenance.primary: Cross-ref Section 07 (clinical prevention) + AF anticoagulation literature; Sharma R, et al. BMJ 2025 stroke treatment review
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; cross-referenced to clinical-prevention section

confidence_notes: The acute reperfusion story is dramatic but the population-level wins are in BP and AF management. Cross-ref Section 07.

statement: With appropriate anti-seizure medication, roughly two-thirds of people with epilepsy become seizure-free; the remaining ~one-third have drug-resistant epilepsy (failure of two adequate trials), for whom surgery, neurostimulation, and dietary therapy are options.
effect_size: ~65-70% seizure-free on ASMs; ~30% drug-resistant
population: Adults with epilepsy (Lancet seminar synthesis)

provenance.primary: Thijs RD, Surges R, O'Brien TJ, Sander JW - 'Epilepsy in adults', Lancet 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Epilepsy surgery for drug-resistant focal epilepsy can be curative and is underused. Ketogenic diet has rct-grade evidence specifically in drug-resistant childhood epilepsy - NOT evidence for keto as a general diet.

statement: Disease-modifying therapies for relapsing multiple sclerosis reduce relapse rates substantially (the most effective, e.g. anti-CD20 B-cell depletion and natalizumab, by ~70-90%), and early high-efficacy treatment preserves long-term function.
effect_size: Annualized relapse-rate reductions ranging from ~30% (interferons) to ~70-90% (high-efficacy mAbs)
population: Relapsing-remitting MS adults (20+ approved DMTs across RCTs)

provenance.primary: Reich DS, Lucchinetti CF, Calabresi PA - 'Multiple Sclerosis', NEJM 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (McDonald criteria: Thompson 2018 10.1016/S1474-4422(17)30470-2)

confidence_notes: A genuine treatment revolution for RELAPSING MS. Honest gaps: progressive MS remains under-served (smoldering neurodegeneration), no cure, real risks (PML, infection). EBV is a near-necessary antecedent. 'MS reversal' diets (Wahls, Swank) are nequals1/anecdotal and must not displace DMTs.

statement: Parkinson's disease has excellent symptomatic treatment (levodopa remains the most effective drug 50+ years on) but NO proven disease-modifying therapy - nothing on the market slows the underlying dopaminergic neurodegeneration.
effect_size: Levodopa: large symptomatic benefit; disease-modification trials uniformly null/unproven to date
population: Parkinson's disease adults (Lancet seminar synthesis)

provenance.primary: Bloem BR, Okun MS, Klein C - 'Parkinson's disease', Lancet 2021
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: The cleanest 'symptom control vs disease modification' honesty gap in the section. Levodopa long-term brings motor fluctuations/dyskinesias; non-dopaminergic features (falls, cognition, dysautonomia) drive late disability regardless. Exercise has rct-grade symptom/function benefit; disease-modification claim is mechanistic/cohort.

statement: Anti-CGRP monoclonal antibodies are the first drug class designed specifically to prevent migraine; they reduce monthly migraine days by roughly 2-3 days more than placebo on average - a meaningful, well-tolerated advance, but not a cure.
effect_size: ~1.5-2.5 fewer monthly migraine days vs placebo (placebo response in migraine is large)
population: Episodic/chronic migraine adults (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, eptinezumab RCTs)

provenance.primary: Edvinsson L, Haanes KA, Warfvinge K, Krause DN - 'CGRP as the target of new migraine therapies - successful translation from bench to clinic', Nat Rev Neurol 2018
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (Ferrari Nat Rev Dis Primers 2022 10.1038/s41572-021-00328-4; Ailani AHS 2021 10.1111/head.14153)

confidence_notes: Real breakthrough but an improvement, not a cure. Modest absolute effect against a large migraine placebo response. Older preventives (propranolol, topiramate, Botox) still work and are far cheaper.

statement: Migraine, tension-type headache, and cluster headache are mechanistically distinct diseases, not severity grades of one thing; conflating them (e.g. treating cluster as migraine) wastes years of patient time.
effect_size: Distinct pathophysiology (trigeminovascular/CGRP vs muscular/stress vs trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia) and distinct treatments (triptans/CGRP vs simple analgesia vs high-flow O2/verapamil)
population: Primary headache disorders (ICHD classification)

provenance.primary: Ferrari MD, et al. - 'Migraine', Nat Rev Dis Primers 2022
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Medication-overuse headache (acute analgesics >10-15 days/month) is one of the most common reversible causes of 'intractable' daily headache - the biggest avoidable harm in headache medicine.

statement: First-line drugs for painful peripheral neuropathy (duloxetine, pregabalin/gabapentin, amitriptyline) have a number-needed-to-treat of roughly 4-8 for 50% pain relief; glycemic control is the only disease-modifying lever for diabetic neuropathy.
effect_size: NNT ~4-8 for 50% pain relief; most patients do not get major relief from any single drug
population: Adults with painful diabetic/peripheral neuropathic pain (NeuPSIG systematic review)

provenance.primary: Finnerup NB, et al. - 'Pharmacotherapy for neuropathic pain in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis', Lancet Neurology 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; cross-ref Section 14 V-nervous-claims (already indexed)

confidence_notes: Genuinely hard to treat. Supplements (alpha-lipoic acid weak/modest, benfotiamine) are oversold; high-dose B6 can itself CAUSE neuropathy. Cross-ref Section 14 6.4.

statement: Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is a real tau neurodegenerative disease caused by repetitive head impacts, but its population risk, dose threshold, and in-life diagnosis are not yet known - the landmark series are autopsy case series with severe selection bias.
effect_size: CTE found in 110/111 examined NFL-player brains (Mez 2017) - but brains donated because disease was suspected (selection bias)
population: Convenience/autopsy samples of contact-sport athletes and military (not population samples)

provenance.primary: Mez J, et al. - 'Clinicopathological Evaluation of Chronic Traumatic Encephalopathy in Players of American Football', JAMA 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; recalled landmark (McKee Brain 2013 10.1093/brain/aws307)

confidence_notes: Both 'CTE is a myth' and 'every concussion causes dementia' overstate the evidence. CTE cannot currently be diagnosed in the living (no validated biomarker). Most single concussions resolve in ~2-4 weeks; modern management is brief rest then graded return.

statement: Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease (cartilage loss + subchondral bone remodeling + synovial inflammation), not simple mechanical wear of inert cartilage; radiographic severity correlates poorly with pain.
effect_size: Active remodeling process; obesity contributes both mechanically and metabolically; X-ray-pain discordance well documented
population: Osteoarthritis (Lancet seminar synthesis)

provenance.primary: Hunter DJ, Bierma-Zeinstra S - 'Osteoarthritis', Lancet 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: The 'wear-and-tear' framing is a trap that drives harmful immobilization of joints that need loading.

statement: First-line osteoarthritis treatment is exercise and weight loss (effect sizes rivaling or beating drugs); there is NO disease-modifying OA drug, and joint replacement is highly effective for end-stage disease while arthroscopic debridement for OA is no better than sham.
effect_size: Exercise/weight-loss: moderate pain/function benefit; arthroscopy for OA: null vs sham; arthroplasty: large function restoration
population: Knee/hip osteoarthritis adults (guideline/meta synthesis)

provenance.primary: Hunter DJ, Bierma-Zeinstra S - 'Osteoarthritis', Lancet 2019
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Glucosamine/chondroitin have at best a small, much-debated (largely null in unbiased trials) effect; low-risk but oversold. The real lever (movement, weight) is unsellable.

statement: Rheumatoid arthritis is now treated to target (escalate from methotrexate to TNF/IL-6/B-cell/JAK-inhibitor therapy until remission/low disease activity), and early treatment within the 'window of opportunity' makes clinical remission a realistic goal.
effect_size: Biologics + treat-to-target: remission now achievable in a large fraction; early treatment preserves joints
population: Rheumatoid arthritis adults (RCT + guideline synthesis)

provenance.primary: Smolen JS, Aletaha D, McInnes IB - 'Rheumatoid arthritis', Lancet 2016
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (mechanism: McInnes & Schett Lancet 2017 10.1016/S0140-6736(17)31472-1)

confidence_notes: A clear biologic-revolution success. Caveats: infection risk (mandatory TB screening), JAKi CV/clot signal in older at-risk patients, cost. Anti-CCP/RF autoantibodies often precede symptoms by years.

statement: Hyperuricemia is dominated by renal under-excretion that is largely genetically determined (SLC2A9, ABCG2); diet raises urate and triggers attacks but contributes only a few percent to serum urate compared with genetics - so 'just change your diet' routinely fails.
effect_size: Dietary contribution to serum urate small (~few %) vs genetic; purine-rich foods/alcohol/fructose raise risk but modestly
population: Men (Health Professionals Follow-up Study) + genetic association studies

provenance.primary: Choi HK, Atkinson K, Karlson EW, Willett W, Curhan G - 'Purine-rich foods, dairy and protein intake, and the risk of gout in men', NEJM 2004
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Corrects the 'rich man's gluttony' framing. Crystals ignite NLRP3 inflammasome -> IL-1-beta (basis of acute attack and IL-1 blockade for refractory cases).

statement: Gout is in principle curable: urate-lowering therapy (allopurinol first-line) titrated to a serum urate target below ~6 mg/dL dissolves crystals and stops the disease - yet it is chronically under-prescribed, under-titrated, and stopped early.
effect_size: Treat-to-target <6 mg/dL: crystal dissolution and attack cessation over months
population: Gout patients with recurrent attacks/tophi/urate stones (ACR 2020 guideline)

provenance.primary: FitzGerald JD, et al. - '2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout', Arthritis Rheumatol 2020
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (febuxostat CV: White CARES NEJM 2018 10.1056/NEJMoa1710895)

confidence_notes: The honest failure is execution: ULT started without colchicine prophylaxis triggers early attacks and patients quit. Febuxostat carries a debated CV-safety signal (CARES).

statement: Hydroxychloroquine is the near-universal backbone of SLE treatment, reducing flares, organ damage, and mortality; it is the one high-value drug for essentially every lupus patient, while the rest of management is organ- and severity-tailored.
effect_size: HCQ associated with fewer flares, less organ damage, lower mortality across cohorts
population: Systemic lupus erythematosus adults (Nat Rev Dis Primers synthesis)

provenance.primary: Kaul A, et al. - 'Systemic lupus erythematosus', Nat Rev Dis Primers 2016
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Type-I interferon signature drives inflammation (basis of belimumab/anifrolumab). Lupus nephritis is the prognosis-defining complication. Chronic glucocorticoid causes much of lupus's long-term damage - minimize dose. CAR-T (Schett Lancet 2023 10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01126-1) is a frontier, not yet standard.

statement: Axial spondyloarthritis is highly treatable (exercise foundational; NSAIDs first-line; TNF and IL-17 inhibitors highly effective), but the dominant failure is diagnostic delay of ~7-10 years from mistaking inflammatory back pain for mechanical back pain.
effect_size: TNF/IL-17 inhibitors: large response in inadequate NSAID responders; IL-23 inhibition works for psoriatic but NOT axial disease
population: Axial/peripheral spondyloarthritis adults (Nat Rev Dis Primers / Nat Rev Rheumatol synthesis)

provenance.primary: Sieper J, Poddubnyy D - 'Axial spondyloarthritis', Nat Rev Dis Primers 2015
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (treatment update: Danve & Deodhar Nat Rev Rheumatol 2022 10.1038/s41584-022-00761-z)

confidence_notes: Pattern to know: back pain WORSE with rest and BETTER with movement, in a young person, >3 months, HLA-B27 - the reverse of mechanical back pain. IL-23-axial dissociation shows the subtypes are mechanistically distinct.

statement: Fibromyalgia is a real disorder of central pain processing (nociplastic pain / central sensitization) with normal inflammatory markers and imaging; 'it's central' is not 'it's imaginary.'
effect_size: Lowered pain thresholds, augmented central responses, impaired descending inhibition
population: Fibromyalgia patients; central-sensitization framework (IASP nociplastic category)

provenance.primary: Woolf CJ - 'Central sensitization: implications for the diagnosis and treatment of pain', Pain 2011
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (review: Siracusa Int J Mol Sci 2021 10.3390/ijms22083891)

confidence_notes: Cross-ref Section 14 6 (central sensitization physiology). The normality of labs/imaging is why it was historically dismissed - a real injustice.

statement: Fibromyalgia's best-supported treatments are graded aerobic exercise (the single strongest), CBT, sleep treatment, and patient education; FDA-approved drugs (duloxetine, milnacipran, pregabalin) help a minority modestly, and opioids are harmful.
effect_size: All effects modest; no single large lever; exercise best-supported
population: Fibromyalgia adults (meta-analytic synthesis)

provenance.primary: Siracusa R, et al. - 'Fibromyalgia: Pathogenesis, Mechanisms, Diagnosis and Treatment Options Update', Int J Mol Sci 2021
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified

confidence_notes: Multimodal, self-management-centered, modest. The genuine levers (exercise, sleep, CBT, validation) are unsellable, so the supplement market dominates instead (see fibromyalgia-supplements-weak).

statement: Polymyalgia rheumatica and giant cell arteritis respond dramatically to glucocorticoids (near-diagnostic); GCA is a medical emergency - high-dose steroids must start immediately on clinical suspicion, before biopsy, to prevent irreversible vision loss.
effect_size: PMR resolves in days on low-dose prednisone; tocilizumab is a proven steroid-sparing agent in GCA
population: Adults over ~50 with PMR/GCA (systematic review + treat-to-target synthesis)

provenance.primary: Buttgereit F, Dejaco C, Matteson EL, Dasgupta B - 'Polymyalgia Rheumatica and Giant Cell Arteritis: A Systematic Review', JAMA 2016
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (treat-to-target: Dejaco Ann Rheum Dis 2024 10.1136/ard-2022-223429)

confidence_notes: The critical clinical rule: new headache + visual symptoms + high inflammatory markers in someone over 50 = treat now, biopsy later. Strong IL-6 signature (basis for tocilizumab and sky-high CRP).

statement: The autoimmune protocol (AIP) elimination diet has only small, mostly uncontrolled pilot evidence (almost all in inflammatory bowel disease) for symptom/quality-of-life improvement; there are no RCTs and no evidence it modifies RA, lupus, MS, or thyroid disease.
effect_size: Small single-arm IBD pilots show symptom/QoL improvement; no controlled disease-modification evidence
population: Mostly IBD pilots (Konijeti 2017 n~15; Chandrasekaran 2019); review across autoimmune diseases

provenance.primary: Konijeti GG, et al. - 'Efficacy of the Autoimmune Protocol Diet for Inflammatory Bowel Disease', Inflamm Bowel Dis 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (review: Pardali Metabol Open 2025 10.1016/j.metop.2024.100342)

confidence_notes: Marketed far beyond its evidence as a treatment for 'all autoimmune disease.' Real harm is using it to REPLACE DMTs/biologics that work; very restrictive, can drive disordered eating and nutrient gaps. Mechanism->outcome overreach.

statement: Prolonged-antibiotic treatment for 'chronic Lyme' (chronic symptoms without evidence of ever having had Lyme, diagnosed by non-validated labs) is refuted by RCTs showing no durable benefit and real harm; this is distinct from post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome (PTLDS), which is real and under-researched.
effect_size: Multiple RCTs of prolonged antibiotics: no durable benefit; harms include line infections and C. difficile
population: Patients with persistent symptoms attributed to Lyme (RCTs + systematic review)

provenance.primary: Dersch R, et al. - 'Treatment of post-treatment Lyme disease symptoms - a systematic review', Eur J Neurol 2024
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; PubMed esearch verified (Beaman Intern Med J 2016 10.1111/imj.13278; Arias guidelines 2025 10.1016/j.idnow.2025.105205)

confidence_notes: Hold both truths: PTLDS (persistent symptoms AFTER documented, treated Lyme) deserves research and compassion; 'chronic Lyme' long-antibiotic protocols are refuted and dangerous. The controversy is genuine but the antibiotic question is settled.

statement: Supplements marketed for fibromyalgia (magnesium, D-ribose, CoQ10, SAMe, 'mitochondrial/adrenal support') have weak, inconsistent, high-bias evidence and no meta-grade support for changing the disease; most present an in-vitro mechanism as a clinical outcome.
effect_size: No supplement has meta-grade support; trials small and high-bias
population: Fibromyalgia supplement trials (heterogeneous, low quality)

provenance.primary: Siracusa R, et al. - 'Fibromyalgia: Pathogenesis, Mechanisms, Diagnosis and Treatment Options Update', Int J Mol Sci 2021 (treatment-evidence synthesis)
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave-24 neuro/rheum disease atlas; mechanism!=outcome grading per SCHEMA.md

confidence_notes: Adjuncts at best; should never displace exercise/CBT/sleep/duloxetine. Same logic applies to most 'natural RA/lupus reversal' protocols. 'Adrenal fatigue' (cross-ref Section 13) is not a real diagnosis.
